intro.author: Paul, according to the letter itself (1:1; 3:1). Traditionally accepted as Paul's; many modern scholars think it was written by a follower in his name.
intro.written: If by Paul, about AD 60–62, while he was a prisoner (3:1; 4:1), traditionally in Rome
intro.audience: Mostly Gentile believers. The words 'at Ephesus' (1:1) are missing from some of the earliest manuscripts, so it may have been a circular letter for several churches in the region.
intro.setting: Ephesus was a leading city of the Roman province of Asia, famous for its huge temple of Artemis (Diana), one of the wonders of the ancient world. Paul had spent about three years there (Acts 20:31). The letter has few personal details, which fits a letter meant to be read in more than one church. Tychicus carried it (6:21).
intro.purpose: To lift readers' eyes to God's plan to unite all things in Christ, and to show how Jews and Gentiles, now one people, should live together.
intro.bigIdea: God has made Jew and Gentile one new people in Christ, called to live worthy of that calling.

outline.title: What God has done in Christ

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE EPHESIANS
